content.summary: Guidance on management of older adults with acute coronary syndromes (ACS). Limited trial data exist for older patients (≈80 years) with NSTE-ACS; invasive strategy showed benefit on composite outcomes in a small RCT but not on all-cause mortality and benefit attenuates with age. For STEMI, primary PCI (PPCI) improves outcomes across ages and should be considered for all STEMI patients; fibrinolysis is reasonable if PPCI cannot be performed timely. Decisions for older patients should be individualized considering ischaemic and bleeding risks, life expectancy, comorbidities, non-cardiac surgery needs, frailty, cognitive and functional status, patient values and preferences. Frailty and multimorbidity are associated with worse outcomes, less frequent use of ACS pharmacotherapy and invasive assessment, longer hospital stays, more complex coronary disease, and higher risk of death and MACE. Invasive management may modestly improve HRQoL up to 1 year, especially in frail and pre-frail patients. There is a lack of robust RCT data to guide care of frail older adults with ACS; a holistic individualized approach is recommended.
recommendations: Individualize management of older patients with ACS based on ischemic/bleeding risks, life expectancy, comorbidities, frailty, cognitive/functional status, and patient preferences.
Consider PPCI for all patients with STEMI; if timely PPCI is not possible, consider fibrinolysis.
Adapt interventional and pharmacological treatments in frail patients after careful evaluation of risks vs benefits.
Assess for multimorbidity and cognitive impairment in older adults referred for coronary angiography, as these increase long-term adverse cardiovascular events and MACE.

frailty_and_multimorbidity.association: Frailty and multimorbidity are linked to adverse outcomes (higher all-cause mortality, MI, stroke, unplanned revascularization, major bleeding), lower use of ACS pharmacotherapies and invasive assessment, longer hospital stays, and poorer baseline HRQoL.
frailty_and_multimorbidity.impact_on_management: Frail patients less frequently receive guideline-directed pharmacotherapy and invasive procedures; invasive management can still offer modest HRQoL benefits, particularly in frail and pre-frail subgroups.
frailty_and_multimorbidity.evidence_gaps: Lack of consensus on optimal frailty assessment tool in older patients with cardiovascular disease and limited RCT data specifically addressing management in frail older adults.

clinical_outcomes_highlighted: Composite outcomes: MI, urgent revascularization, stroke, death
content.notes: Supplementary pharmacotherapy details for older patients are referenced in supplementary data online. Several numbered references cited throughout the text indicate limited and variable quality evidence.
